quests.instruction: Pass the information on, keeping only what matters. Include the three key words.
quests.prompt: Summarize a work or study meeting you attended in two sentences.
quests.sampleAnswer: We discussed the new timetable and agreed to test it for a month. The next step is collecting feedback from everyone.
quests.hint: Cover what was discussed, what was decided, and what happens next.
quests.explanation: A good summary has three parts: topic, decision, and next action. It leaves out who said what.

quests.instruction: Summarize the key information in a single sentence. Make sure all three words fit the meaning.
quests.prompt: A technician visited to repair your heating. Summarize what he found and did.
quests.sampleAnswer: The technician found a broken valve, replaced it, and the heating is working normally again.
quests.hint: Use three past-tense verbs in a chain: what he found, what he did, and the result.
quests.explanation: Summaries of events use past tense for actions and end with the present result, so the reader knows the current situation.

quests.instruction: Pass the information on in one clear sentence, keeping only what matters. Work in each of the three words.
quests.prompt: You watched a short video about saving energy at home. Give its main point.
quests.sampleAnswer: The video's main point was that small changes, like switching off standby devices, can noticeably reduce your electricity bill.
quests.hint: State the main idea in one sentence and add one example from the video.
quests.explanation: A summary states the main idea in your own words, and one example shows that you understood it.

quests.instruction: Write an evaluation in one or two sentences that weighs both sides. Make sure all three words fit the meaning.
quests.prompt: A small café is deciding whether to accept only card payments. Weigh it up and recommend.
quests.sampleAnswer: Card-only payment is faster and safer for staff, but some customers only carry cash. I recommend accepting both until most customers switch.
quests.hint: Give one benefit, one drawback, then your recommendation.
quests.explanation: A recommendation is stronger after you have weighed both sides, because the reader can see why you chose it.

quests.instruction: Judge the option in one or two sentences and support your judgment. Include the three key words.
quests.prompt: Weigh up working four long days a week against five shorter days.
quests.sampleAnswer: Four longer days give you an extra day off, but the tiring hours could reduce your productivity. For most people I think the benefits outweigh the costs.
quests.hint: Use 'outweigh' to show which side is heavier for you.
quests.explanation: 'Outweigh' expresses a judgment between pros and cons in one word, which is a useful skill in evaluation.

quests.instruction: Judge the option in a single sentence and support your judgment. Fit the three key words into your answer naturally.
quests.prompt: A friend is visiting a big city for a week. Weigh renting a car against using public transport.
quests.sampleAnswer: Renting a car gives you freedom, but parking is expensive, so public transport is usually worth choosing in a big city.
quests.hint: Weigh the two options and end with a clear conclusion.
quests.explanation: Ending with a conclusion turns a comparison into advice the friend can act on.

quests.instruction: Reflect in one clear sentence on what you learned. Each word should appear in your answer.
quests.prompt: Say how a change in your evening phone habits has changed your sleep, or how it might.
quests.sampleAnswer: Since I stopped using my phone in bed, I've noticed that I fall asleep faster and feel less tired the next day.
quests.hint: Use 'noticed' for an observation and connect it to the habit change.
quests.explanation: 'Noticed' presents a result as something you observed, which sounds honest and not exaggerated.

quests.instruction: Reflect in one clear sentence on what you learned. Include the three key words.
quests.prompt: Describe what you learned when you started keeping track of your spending.
quests.sampleAnswer: I started tracking my spending in an app, and I quickly realized how much I was spending on small daily purchases.
quests.hint: Say what you started doing and what it showed you.
quests.explanation: A habit change is most interesting when it reveals something surprising, and 'realized' shows the moment your understanding changed.

quests.instruction: Say how the two things differ in one clear sentence. Include all three key words.
quests.prompt: Describe how your way of learning new words has changed.
quests.sampleAnswer: Instead of memorizing lists, I now practice speaking with a partner, which helps me remember words in real situations.
quests.hint: Use 'instead of' to contrast old and new methods.
quests.explanation: 'Instead of' names the replaced habit and lets you explain the benefit of the new one.

quests.instruction: Explain the cause and its effect in one clear sentence. Include the three key words.
quests.prompt: An online shop's website crashed during a big sale. Explain why.
quests.sampleAnswer: The site crashed because it was overloaded by too many visitors arriving at the same time.
quests.hint: Use the passive 'was overloaded' to describe what happened to the site.
quests.explanation: The passive focuses on what happened to the site, which suits technical explanations.

quests.instruction: Show how one thing leads to another in a single sentence. Work in each of the three words.
quests.prompt: Describe the effect on customers and on the business.
quests.sampleAnswer: Many customers abandoned their orders, and the support team received hundreds of complaints within an hour.
quests.hint: Give one effect on customers and one on the company.
quests.explanation: Showing effects on two groups, customers and the company, gives a fuller picture of the consequences than describing only one side.

quests.instruction: Name the issue and offer a solution in one sentence. Each word should appear in your answer.
quests.prompt: Recommend how the company can prevent this next time.
quests.sampleAnswer: To prevent this next time, the company should add more servers and test the site before every big sale.
quests.hint: Use 'To prevent' plus a recommendation with 'should'.
quests.explanation: 'To + verb' at the start of a sentence states a purpose, and 'should' gives a clear recommendation.

quests.instruction: Explain in one clear sentence so the reason is easy to follow. Your answer should contain all three key words.
quests.prompt: Claim that some jobs need more creativity than people think, and give an example.
quests.sampleAnswer: Even an accountant needs creativity, for example when explaining complicated numbers in a simple way.
quests.hint: Choose a job people think is not creative and show where creativity appears.
quests.explanation: A surprising example makes a claim memorable, and 'even' shows that the example is unexpected.

quests.instruction: Explain in one sentence so the reason is easy to follow. Use the three words meaningfully.
quests.prompt: Give an example of how formal and informal writing differ in daily life.
quests.sampleAnswer: Emails to a manager are usually formal, whereas messages to friends can be short and casual.
quests.hint: Use 'whereas' to set two real examples side by side, such as a manager and a friend.
quests.explanation: Concrete examples such as a manager and a friend make an abstract distinction between formal and informal writing easy to see.

quests.instruction: Explain in two short sentences so the reason is easy to follow. Include the three key words.
quests.prompt: Say technology can make life harder, and give an example.
quests.sampleAnswer: Technology can make life harder. For instance, constant notifications interrupt your work and make it difficult to concentrate.
quests.hint: State the claim in one sentence and give a specific example in the next.
quests.explanation: Claim then example is a strong two-sentence structure: the first sentence tells the reader what you think and the second proves it.

quests.instruction: Say how the two things differ in one or two sentences. Make sure all three words fit the meaning.
quests.prompt: Compare shops today with shops fifty years ago.
quests.sampleAnswer: Many people no longer visit shops for everyday items, whereas fifty years ago most purchases were made in person. Now much of it happens online.
quests.hint: Use 'no longer' for what has stopped and 'whereas' to contrast.
quests.explanation: 'No longer' shows a change from the past, and 'whereas' sets old and new side by side.

quests.instruction: Compare the two options in one sentence. Use the three words meaningfully.
quests.prompt: Compare how travelers planned trips in the past with how they plan today.
quests.sampleAnswer: Travelers used to rely on printed guidebooks, but nowadays they can check reviews and prices instantly on their phones.
quests.hint: Say what they used to do, then what they can do now.
quests.explanation: 'Nowadays' signals the present situation and works with 'used to' for the past.

quests.instruction: Compare the two options in one clear sentence. Each word should appear in your answer.
quests.prompt: Compare how workplaces handled documents in the past with today.
quests.sampleAnswer: Documents were once kept on paper in large archives, but today most are scanned and stored digitally.
quests.hint: Use one past-tense verb form and one present-tense one.
quests.explanation: Passive verbs (are scanned, are stored) fit descriptions of processes when the actors are not important.

quests.instruction: Give clear instructions in a single sentence. Work in each of the three words.
quests.prompt: Explain how to clean a laptop screen safely.
quests.sampleAnswer: Switch off the laptop, wipe the screen gently with a soft cloth, and avoid spraying liquid directly onto it.
quests.hint: Give the steps in order and include one thing to avoid.
quests.explanation: Instructions with one warning prevent the most common mistake, which is spraying liquid straight on the screen.

quests.instruction: Tell the person what to do in one sentence, in order. Include all three key words.
quests.prompt: Explain how to back up photos before deleting them from your phone.
quests.sampleAnswer: Before deleting photos from your phone, copy them to your computer or cloud storage, and check that they open correctly.
quests.hint: Start with 'Before' to show the required order.
quests.explanation: 'Before' plus an -ing form sets the order of actions, and the final check prevents data loss.

quests.instruction: Give clear instructions in a single sentence. Your answer should contain all three key words.
quests.prompt: Explain how to lift a heavy box without hurting your back.
quests.sampleAnswer: Bend your knees, keep the box close to your body, and avoid twisting while you lift, or you could hurt your back.
quests.hint: Combine steps and a warning with 'or' to explain the risk.
quests.explanation: 'Or' plus a consequence gives the reader a reason to follow the instructions, because they can see the risk of ignoring them.

quests.instruction: Write a brief summary in one sentence for someone who missed it. Use all three words naturally.
quests.prompt: In a survey, 70% of students said they study best in the morning, 20% in the evening, 10% had no preference. Summarize and draw a conclusion.
quests.sampleAnswer: The majority of students prefer studying in the morning, which suggests that classes might work better early in the day.
quests.hint: State the main result and add what it suggests.
quests.explanation: 'Suggests' introduces a cautious conclusion, which is right when data shows a pattern but does not prove it.

quests.instruction: Summarize the key information in one sentence. Make sure all three words fit the meaning.
quests.prompt: Umbrella sales rose 40% in October, the rainiest month. Explain what the data shows.
quests.sampleAnswer: Umbrella sales rose by 40% in October, the rainiest month, which shows a clear link between weather and demand.
quests.hint: Connect two facts from the data, the sales increase and the rainy month, in one sentence.
quests.explanation: Linking two data points shows that you understand what the numbers mean, not just that you can repeat them.

quests.instruction: Pass the information on in one clear sentence, keeping only what matters. Work in each of the three words.
quests.prompt: After a café introduced free Wi-Fi, customers stayed about thirty minutes longer. Explain the likely reason.
quests.sampleAnswer: After the café introduced free Wi-Fi, customers stayed about thirty minutes longer, and the likely reason is that they were using it to work.
quests.hint: Report the change first, then use 'likely' to offer a cautious explanation.
quests.explanation: 'Likely' offers an explanation without claiming certainty, which is how careful writers handle data.

quests.instruction: Make the meaning clear in a single sentence. Each word should appear in your answer.
quests.prompt: Explain inflation to a friend who has never studied economics.
quests.sampleAnswer: Inflation means that prices rise over time, so the same amount of money buys less than it did before.
quests.hint: Define the term in one clause and then explain what it means for a person.
quests.explanation: A good explanation gives the definition first and its personal effect second, so a beginner sees why the idea matters to them.

quests.instruction: Clarify in one clear sentence so nothing is confusing. Work in each of the three words.
quests.prompt: Explain what cloud storage is to someone who only saves files on a computer.
quests.sampleAnswer: Cloud storage means your files are saved on servers on the internet, so you can access them from any device.
quests.hint: Explain where the files are and what that allows.
quests.explanation: Explaining where the files are and what that allows makes a technical term easy to understand without technical language.

quests.instruction: Clarify in one clear sentence so nothing is confusing. Your answer should contain all three key words.
quests.prompt: Explain what a refund is to a person who is shopping online for the first time.
quests.sampleAnswer: A refund means the money is returned to you, usually to your original payment method, when you send something back.
quests.hint: Explain what happens, who receives the money, and how it usually arrives.
quests.explanation: A short definition plus one detail (the original payment method) answers the practical question people have.

quests.instruction: Share the experience in one clear sentence. Use the three words meaningfully.
quests.prompt: Describe one thing that gradually changed during your first year in a new job, course, or place.
quests.sampleAnswer: Gradually I felt more confident, and my colleagues started giving me more responsibilities.
quests.hint: Use 'gradually' to show slow change, then name a concrete effect that others could see.
quests.explanation: 'Gradually' makes it clear that the change happened slowly, and naming the effect makes it concrete.

quests.instruction: Write what this taught you in one sentence. Work in each of the three words.
quests.prompt: Say what you struggled with most that year and how you handled it.
quests.sampleAnswer: I struggled with the fast pace, so I asked more experienced colleagues for advice and eventually developed my own routine.
quests.hint: Name the problem, what you did, and how it ended.
quests.explanation: A three-part answer (problem, action, result) is the basic structure of most reflective writing.

quests.instruction: Give a recommendation in one sentence and say why. Use the three words meaningfully.
quests.prompt: Give advice to the next person joining the same job or course.
quests.sampleAnswer: I would advise newcomers to ask questions early and to be patient with themselves, because everyone needs time to learn.
quests.hint: Use 'I would advise' and give two pieces of advice.
quests.explanation: 'I would advise' is a polite recommendation, and a reason at the end makes it convincing.
